blocks.title: dbx-pro — a full database workbench inside Astravia
blocks.description: Manage connections, browse schemas, write and run SQL, inspect sortable result grids, and let AI call your database directly. Reads go through dbx-mcp for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, ClickHouse and 100+ databases; writes and DDL run through bundled drivers.

items.title: Connection manager
items.description: Store host, port, database and environment labels with read-only / production flags; passwords live in the host's encrypted credential vault, never as plaintext.

items.title: SQL editor
items.description: Multi-tab CodeMirror editor with per-dialect highlighting and autocomplete; run with ⌘/Ctrl+Enter, or execute just the selection.

items.title: Result grid
items.description: Sort by header, paginate, keep row numbers, copy TSV / export CSV and inspect cells, with row count and duration shown.

items.title: DDL and writes
items.description: Create and alter tables through bundled pg / mysql2 / mssql drivers; a full-SQL confirmation appears first and read-only connections are rejected outright.

items.title: Query history
items.description: Each query logs its SQL, status, row count and duration (no result rows stored), ready to reload and rerun in the editor.

items.title: Bidirectional AI
items.description: The plugin registers as an MCP tool so AI can list connections and run queries; you can also send tree or result context to AI in one click.

items.title: Open the workbench
items.description: Install dbx-pro from the marketplace and open its activity tab. The engine comes up with the plugin — no separate CLI install.

items.title: Add a connection
items.description: Click "Connect" in the top right, pick a database type and fill it in; for SQLite just choose a file.

items.title: Run a query
items.description: Type SQL and press ⌘/Ctrl+Enter; confirm when the statement writes or changes schema.

blocks.content: Reads use dbx-mcp while writes and DDL use the plugin's bundled drivers; the two paths are isolated. Every service listens on loopback only and is never exposed to the network.
